text: In their search for wisdom, they study the old writings, especially those of the prophets.[90]
These teachers learn the sayings of famous people and understand the meaning of stories,
even those parts that are difficult. And they look for the meaning hidden in a proverb.
They give advice to leaders, and they travel in other countries to see the good and the bad done there.
These teachers get up early to pray to the Lord Most High, their Creator— they tell him what they need and ask that their sins be forgiven.
The great Lord may choose to give special understanding to a teacher's mind. Such teachers will pray and thank the Lord for the wise advice that they now can give.
They will study those things the Lord has kept secret. He will help them learn and tell them what to say,
and they will teach what they have learned. They will be proud of the Lord's Law and agreement with Israel.
Their understanding will be praised by many, and their names remembered for all time.
Israel will honor them, and other nations will admire their wisdom.
If they live to old age, they will be famous, and if not, they will be content to be at rest.[91]
I have hardly begun to tell you all the things I want to say.
You, my students, are faithful to God, so listen, and you will blossom like rose bushes planted beside a stream.
You will grow faster than lilies, and your songs praising the Lord for what he has done will be a pleasant smell, spreading like incense.
So play your harps and sing praises to the Lord. Give honor to him with this song:
“Everything the Lord does is very good, and his commands will be obeyed at the right moment.
For now, we must not question what God has done, but he has set a time to explain everything. He created places for all the water, and when he commanded the sea, it piled up like a wall.
When he gives an order, it is obeyed, and no one can stop him when he decides to rescue.
“We can't hide from God; he has watched everything that each human has done.
He sees the past and the future; there is nothing he cannot do.
So don't question what God has done; he had a purpose in mind for each thing he created.
“God will bless us greatly, like a river that overflows and soaks the dry ground.
But the Gentiles will feel his anger, as he makes their fresh water too salty to drink.
God lets his people walk on a straight pathway, but those who reject his laws will find that their path is lined with hidden traps.
From the very beginning God prepared good things for good people, and horrible things for sinners.
“What do we need for daily life? Iron tools, water, and fire; flour, milk, and honey, wine, olive oil, and salt; and, of course, clothing.
All of these are good for God's loyal people but become evil in the hands of sinners.
“The Lord created furious winds to take revenge for him. And on the day of judgment, they will punish his enemies, then his anger will be calmed. *
God also created other things to take revenge for him— fire and hail, along with famine and deadly diseases,
wild animals and scorpions, and poisonous snakes, not to mention war.
They are ready to serve him, and at his command, they gladly and quickly obey.”
I have believed all these things since my childhood, but I thought deeply about them before I wrote them down in that song.
The Lord made only good things, and at the right time he will give us what we need.
Everything he created has its own purpose, and so, you cannot say, “This is better than that.”
Sing praises to the Lord with all your heart, and give him thanks!
